messages:
sam_connor: FYI I'm leaving shift at 07:00 UTC. There's an active Sev2 for text-gen-west (elevated p95 latency + some 5xxs). Current state: mitigation in progress, we've rolled a non-disruptive config change (cache TTL tweak) and enabled fallback routing to model-embed-1. I need to hand off ownership before I step out. Who can drive and who will own external comms? Link to incident: https://incidents.internal/company/INC-20240520-47 and runbook: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/text-gen-latency

maria_ops: I can own comms until 09:00 UTC. Happy to keep SLO/status updates and update the status page. I'll be reachable on pager and email. :thumbsup:

lee_oncall: I can drive the incident after 06:55 UTC (takeover at 07:00). I'll keep the console and coord with infra. Note: backup secondary (pranav) is OOO until 09:00, so we have a coverage gap for escalation.

sam_connor: Thanks @lee_oncall and @maria_ops. Assigning roles: driver=lee_oncall, comms=maria_ops. Secondary escalation gap noted (pranav OOO until 09:00). Leaving these runbook pointers in the thread:
- Short runbook (triage): https://wiki.internal/runbooks/text-gen-latency#shortplay
- Postmortem template & comms: https://wiki.internal/incidents/postmortem-template

oncall-bot: NOTE: Please formally claim roles with the incident tool. To claim from Slack run:
```
/incident assign --incident INC-20240520-47 --driver lee_oncall --comms maria_ops
```
I'll persist roles to the incident tracker once the command runs.

maria_ops: Running the command now. I'll post the initial customer-facing note with the usual template (short blurb, affected regions, ETA):
```
We are investigating elevated latency in text generation for customers in US-West. Engineers are actively mitigating. No data loss expected. Next update in 15 minutes or when service stabilizes.
```
I'll also pin the status page and add a link to this thread.

lee_oncall: Taking over console. Actions I'm performing now:
1) tailing task logs across the pool: `kubectl logs -f deploy/text-gen-west --since=10m`
2) checking node GPU load and scheduler: `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output` (infra notified)
3) temporarily increasing worker pool by +1 replica to absorb load: `kubectl scale deploy/text-gen-west --replicas=6`
4) forcing fallback model variant for requests > 5s via router flag (non-disruptive).
I'll report back when each step completes.

sam_connor: Quick notes before I go: KV cache warming was inconsistent; we saw a small spike in cold-starts hitting the heavier model. Fallback triggered once around 06:20 but metrics improved after TTL tweak. No customer-facing errors yet other than latency. If latency persists after scaling, escalate to infra (tag: @infra-escalate).

sre_bot: Auto-note: handoff recorded — outgoing:oncall=sam_connor, incoming:oncall=lee_oncall, comms_owner=maria_ops, incident=INC-20240520-47, recorded_at=1716204823.

maria_ops: Posted customer message and pinned status. Next update scheduled in 12 minutes. Also flagged the account team for high-value customers affected (cc: @acct_team).

lee_oncall: Scale complete. Observed GPU util drop from 92% -> 68% on one hot node. p95 latency dropped ~15% after replica increase but still ~10% above SLO. Proceeding to check model cache hit rates and KV shard distribution. If we don't see improvement in 10m we'll consider a temporary routing to model-compact-quantized as a fall-through.

sam_connor: Great handoff. Leaving a short checklist for whoever picks this up next:
- Confirm roles in incident tool (/incident assign)
- Keep comms cadence: 15m updates or on material changes
- Document all config changes in the incident tracker (so rollback is possible)
- Note coverage gap until 09:00 UTC in the tracker and call in security/infra if escalation needed

lee_oncall: Acknowledged. I'll drive and update the incident tracker as we progress.

maria_ops: Acknowledged. I'll own customer and internal comms.

sre_bot: Hand-off complete. If anyone else wants to join as secondary, reply here and we'll update the incident record.
